Relevant Provisions of law:
Section 342 IPC provides - punishment for wrongful confinement "Whoever wrongfully confines any person shall be punished with simple imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both."

Section 392 IPC provides - punishment for robbery - "whoever commits robbery shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and, if the robbery be committed on the highway between sunset and sunrise, the imprisonment may be extended to fourteen years"
Section 397 IPC provides as under:-
"Enhanced punishment in certain cases of robbery ie., - if, at the time of committing robbery or dacoity, the offender used any deadly weapon, or causes grievous hurt to any person, or attempts to cause death or grievous hurt to any person, the imprisonment with which such offender shall be punished shall not be less than seven years."

Discussion on Merits:-
23. Having considered the relevant law and the settled principal with respect to the offences with which the accused has been charged with, I shall proceed with examining the evidence on record.
24.
When complainant deposed before the Court, he stated that he had seen the face of one accused person as his mask was coming off frequently.
However, when he was shown both the accused in the Court, he could not identify them stating that the person who committed robbery in his house was not present in the Court.
As per his deposition, crime team had visited the spot and lifted fingerprints.
25. PW2 HC Ajit Singh, crime team deposed that two chance-prints were recovered from the spot.
As per report dated 26.06.2023 of the Finger Print Bureau, Crime Branch, the chance-prints lifted from the spot did not match with palm prints of any of accused.
The said report is now Ex.X1 for purpose of reference.
26. As per the deposition of PW5/ IO/ SI Varun, accused Mohd. Chand got recovered a desi katta from Batla House.
The site plan of place of recovery is Ex.PW5/P11, the pointing out memo is Ex.PW5/P8.
As per the site plan of recovery, the place of recovery was adjacent to a constructed building and the area was shown as Batla House.

The IO has not mentioned PS Jamia Nagar State v.
Mohd. Chand & Ors. Page no. 16 of 18 the address of the building/ house in front of which the katta is shown to be allegedly recovered.

sentences.text: As such, the place of recovery is not clearly identified but prima facie appears to be a residential area.
At the time of recovery, he was accompanied by PW8/ HC Manveer.
During his cross-examination, PW8 HC Manveer had admitted that the place of recovery of the weapon from accused Mohd. Chand was a Jungle and there was no residence or market nearby.
He has contradicted the testimony of PW5 / IO / SI Varun with respect to the place of recovery.
The contradiction is material in nature and has remained unexplained.
It goes to the root of the case.
In these circumstances, reasonable doubt arises out regarding the recovery of the alleged country-made pistol from the possession of the accused Mohd. Chand.

State vs Mohd. Chand on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127913530/
10 27.
Further, no robbed article has been recovered from the possession of any accused in the present case.
There is no evidence to link either accused to the alleged robbery.
There is nothing on record to establish the culpability of the accused persons in the commission of the offence charged against them.

It is cardinal principle of criminal jurisprudence that prosecution has to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and if any doubt has been created then benefit of it should be given to the accused persons.
The prosecution has failed to prove the charge on the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, accused Mohd. Chand S/o Mohd. Murtaza and accused Saheem Khan @ Bhola S/o Sh. Wahid are acquitted PS Jamia Nagar State v. Mohd. Chand & Ors.

opennyai_summary.facts:
On 21.06.2017, 3-4 masked persons entered the house of complainant Bisrat Hussain between 9-9:15 AM.
The house of the complainant was already unlocked.
All the masked persons were armed with country-made pistols and knife like object.
They asked complainant to hand-over all the valuables to them in the presence of his wife Dr. Azra Khan and two kids.
Dr. Azra Khan handed-over her ring, earrings and 10- 12 thousand cash.
The accused took two mobile phones from them.
They had locked complainant, his wife and two kids in the room while they searched for valuables in other rooms.
Matter was reported to police and FIR was registered.
The copy of the charge-sheet was supplied to the accused in compliance of Section 207 Cr.PC.
After this, prosecution evidence was closed and matter was listed for examination of accused Under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

At the time of recovery, he was accompanied by PW8/ HC Manveer.
During his cross-examination, PW8 HC Manveer had admitted that the place of recovery of the weapon from accused Mohd. Chand was a Jungle and there was no residence or market nearby.
He has contradicted the testimony of PW5 / IO / SI Varun with respect to the place of recovery.
The contradiction is material in nature and has remained unexplained.

Further, no robbed article has been recovered from the possession of any accused in the present case.
There is no evidence to link either accused to the alleged robbery.
There is nothing on record to establish the culpability of the accused persons in the commission of the offence charged against them.
It is cardinal principle of criminal jurisprudence that prosecution has to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and if any doubt has been created then benefit of it should be given to the accused persons.
The prosecution has failed to prove the charge on the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt.
